courses.name: Object-Oriented Programming I
courses.description: Introduction to programming and computer science. Emphasizes understanding and implementation of applications using object-oriented techniques.
courses.notes: Exemption exam available

courses.name: Object-Oriented Programming II
courses.description: Introduction to use of computers to solve problems using software engineering principles. Design, build, test, and debug medium -size software systems and learn to use relevant tools.
courses.notes: Exemption exam available

courses.name: Introduction to Computer Systems
courses.description: Introduction to the interaction between user programs and the operating system/hardware. Major topics include C programming, introductory systems programming, and assembly language.
courses.notes: Exemption exam available

courses.name: Discrete Structures
courses.description: Fundamental mathematical concepts related to computer science, including finite and infinite sets, relations, functions, and propositional logic. Introduction to other techniques, modeling and solving problems in computer science.
courses.notes: Exemption exam available

courses.name: Organization of Programming Languages
courses.description: A study of programming languages, including their syntax, semantics, and implementation. Several different models of languages are discussed.
courses.notes: Required for 75-credit benchmark

courses.name: Algorithms
courses.description: A systematic study of the complexity of some elementary algorithms related to sorting, graphs and trees, and combinatorics. Algorithms are analyzed using mathematical techniques to solve recurrences and summations.
courses.notes: Required for 75-credit benchmark

courses.name: Introduction to Data Science
courses.description: An introduction to data science. Provides a comprehensive view of the data management, analysis, and modeling process. Topics include data acquisition, cleaning, management, exploratory analysis, and visualization.
courses.notes: Does not count toward distributive area

courses.name: Computer Systems Architecture
courses.description: Introduction to computer systems architecture. Topics include performance metrics, instruction set design, pipelining, cache design, memory systems, input/output systems, and modern architectural features.
courses.notes: Area 1: Systems

courses.name: Operating Systems
courses.description: A hands-on introduction to operating systems, including topics in: multiprogramming, communication and synchronization, memory management, IO subsystems, and resource scheduling policies.
courses.notes: Area 1: Systems. Has unique prerequisites/registration requirements.

courses.name: Computer and Network Security
courses.description: An introduction to the topic of security in the context of computer systems and networks. Identify, analyze, and solve network-related security problems in computer systems.
courses.notes: Area 1: Systems

courses.name: Computer Networks
courses.description: Computer networks and architectures. Underlying design principles. Protocols. Focuses on the Internet and related protocols.
courses.notes: Area 1: Systems

courses.name: Data Structures
courses.description: Description, properties, and storage allocation functions of data structures including lists, trees, graphs, tables, and sets.
courses.notes: Area 2: Information Processing

courses.name: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Introduces a range of ideas and methods in AI, varying semester to semester but chosen largely from: search, planning, knowledge representation, reasoning, decision-making under uncertainty, machine learning, natural language, robotics, perception, and action.
courses.notes: Area 2: Information Processing. Popular elective for Robotics minor.

courses.name: Introduction to Machine Learning
courses.description: Machine learning studies the problem of how to build programs that improve their performance at some task through experience. This course surveys a wide variety of approaches in machine learning.
courses.notes: Area 2: Information Processing. Has unique prerequisites. Popular elective for Robotics minor.

courses.name: Database Design
courses.description: An introduction to the design of databases and their use in database management systems. Topics include entity-relationship and relational models, normalization theory, query languages, query optimization, and concurrency control.
courses.notes: Area 2: Information Processing

courses.name: Computer Vision
courses.description: An introduction to basic concepts and techniques in computer vision. Topics include image formation, edge detection, texture analysis, color, stereo vision, and motion.
courses.notes: Area 2: Information Processing. Has unique prerequisites. Elective for Robotics minor.

courses.name: Introduction to Compilers
courses.description: Topics include lexical analysis, parsing, intermediate representations, program analysis, optimization, and code generation.
courses.notes: Area 3: Software Engineering and Programming Languages

courses.name: Programming Language Technologies and Paradigms
courses.description: Provides an introduction to a selection of programming language technologies and paradigms. Possible topics include scripting languages, declarative programming, visual languages, concurrent programming, and domain-specific languages.
courses.notes: Area 3: Software Engineering and Programming Languages

courses.name: Introduction to Human-Computer Interaction
courses.description: Designing, implementing, and evaluating user interfaces. Understand something about the nature of human-machine interaction and apply that understanding to user interface design and implementation.
courses.notes: Area 3: Software Engineering and Programming Languages

courses.name: Software Engineering
courses.description: Object oriented software development. Topics include functional requirements, use cases, UML diagrams, design patterns, software development processes, testing, and maintenance.
courses.notes: Area 3: Software Engineering and Programming Languages. Has unique prerequisites.

courses.name: Design and Analysis of Computer Algorithms
courses.description: Fundamental techniques for designing efficient algorithms and basic mathematical tools for analyzing their performance.
courses.notes: Area 4: Theory. Elective for Robotics minor.

courses.name: Elementary Theory of Computation
courses.description: Introduction to formal languages and automata, computability and uncomputability, and rudiments of computational complexity theory.
courses.notes: Area 4: Theory

courses.name: Cryptology
courses.description: An introduction to modern cryptography. Various symmetric and asymmetric key cryptographic functions and protocols will be covered.
courses.notes: Area 4: Theory. Has unique prerequisites.

courses.name: Computational Methods
courses.description: Significant figures, errors, IEEE arithmetic, root finding, polynomial interpolation, integration, solution of linear and nonlinear systems of equations, least squares, solution of differential equations.
restrictions: Credit only given for CMSC460 or CMSC466, not both
courses.notes: Area 5: Numerical Analysis. Has unique prerequisites.

courses.name: Introduction to Numerical Analysis
courses.description: Introduction to numerical analysis with emphasis on algorithms and their analysis. Error analysis, polynomial interpolation, iterative methods for non-linear equations, numerical differentiation and integration, and initial value problems in ordinary differential equations.
restrictions: Credit only given for CMSC466 or CMSC460, not both
courses.notes: Area 5: Numerical Analysis. Has unique prerequisites.

courses.name: Robotics Perception and Planning
courses.description: Fundamentals of robot perception and robot path planning including planning, control, velocity dynamics, graph-based planning, Bayesian filtering, camera models, visual perception, and machine learning.
restrictions: Must be in Robotics and Autonomous Systems minor or permission
courses.notes: Core course for Robotics minor. Has unique prerequisites. Does not count toward CS distributive areas.
